title: Fix Jap Section Bugs, Smooth Nam Jap Counting & Add Progress Bar

requirements.summary: Fix all bugs in the Jap section: resolve state management issues causing incorrect count display, fix tap handler debouncing/double-counting, ensure session and daily counts update correctly, and prevent race conditions between local state and backend sync
acceptanceCriteria: Every single tap/press increments the displayed nam jap count by exactly 1 with no skips or double-counts
Session count and daily count remain consistent with each other and do not reset unexpectedly mid-session
Rapid repeated taps are handled gracefully without freezing, skipping counts, or crashing
Backend sync does not override or revert the locally displayed count while the user is actively chanting
Milestone effects (ripple, lotus bloom at 108) trigger at the correct count values

file_operations.description: Refactor state management to use a useRef for immediate local count tracking (optimistic updates) separate from the React state used for rendering. Replace the current useState count with a ref-based counter that increments synchronously on tap, then schedules a state update. Remove any debouncing from the tap handler itself. Ensure the tapCount state and dailyCount from backend stay in sync by reconciling them only when the component mounts or when backend data changes (not during active tapping). Fix any race conditions by preventing backend sync responses from overwriting the local ref counter while user is actively chanting. Verify milestone triggers (ripple at each tap, lotus bloom at 108) fire at the correct count values by checking the ref counter value.

requirements.summary: Implement smooth, lag-free nam jap counting: use optimistic local state updates (increment immediately on tap) and debounce/batch backend sync calls to prevent UI jank from excessive re-renders or network requests
acceptanceCriteria: The counter number updates visually within 16ms (one animation frame) of each tap
No visible stutter, lag, or delay when tapping rapidly
Backend sync is batched/debounced and does not cause the counter to flicker or temporarily revert

file_operations.description: Implement optimistic UI updates: on tap, immediately increment a local useRef counter and update the displayed count state synchronously (or via a microtask) without waiting for backend. Introduce a debounced backend sync function (using a timer or a library like lodash.debounce) that batches increments and calls the backend incrementJap mutation only after a short delay (e.g., 500ms) since the last tap. Ensure the displayed count always reflects the local ref, and backend sync happens in the background. Prevent backend responses or refetches from causing the counter to flicker by ignoring stale backend data during active tapping sessions. Test rapid tapping to confirm no stutter or lag in the visual counter update.

requirements.summary: Add a circular or linear progress bar to the Jap section that fills from 0 to 108 as the count increases, resets for each mala cycle, displays current/target count, and uses saffron/gold devotional colors
acceptanceCriteria: A progress bar is visible on the Jap page that fills from 0% to 100% as the count goes from 0 to 108
Progress bar resets and refills for each new 108-count mala cycle
Current count and target (e.g., '45 / 108') are displayed near the progress bar
Progress bar color uses saffron or gold tones matching the app's devotional theme
Progress bar updates smoothly and instantly in sync with each tap

file_operations.description: Add a progress bar component (circular or linear) below or near the main tap counter that visualizes progress from 0 to 108. Calculate the progress percentage as (currentCount % 108) / 108 * 100. Render a progress indicator using a <div> with a linear gradient (for linear bar) or an SVG circle stroke (for circular bar) styled with saffron (#FF9933) or gold gradient colors from the theme. Display the text '(currentCount % 108) / 108' adjacent to or inside the progress bar. Ensure the progress bar updates immediately when the local count ref changes (not waiting for backend sync). When the count reaches a multiple of 108, the progress bar should smoothly reset to 0 and begin filling again. Use CSS transitions or animations to make the fill smooth. Position the progress bar prominently on the Jap page, ensuring it does not obstruct the main tap button or visual effects.
